name: Bring Back the Mug
summary: Durnan Furcutter sends you back across Coldridge Valley with Nori Pridedrift's empty mug. Its return closes the Mornbrew delivery.

sections.title: A Matter of Tavern Etiquette
sections.body: After warming himself with the Mornbrew, Durnan leaves the tankard in your care. Cold bites hard in Dun Morogh, where hospitality depends on mutual respect. Good dishware should make it back too.

sections.title: Mugs Don't Grow on Trees
sections.body: Nori Pridedrift values sturdy drinkware. Mugs do not grow on trees, especially among the subzero crags of the dwarven homeland. Bring his mug back in one piece, and you show the local community that you can be trusted.

aliases: who gives bring back the mug
faq.answer: After you deliver the freshly brewed Mornbrew to Durnan Furcutter in Dun Morogh, he sends you back with the empty tankard.

faq.q: Who do I return the mug to?
aliases: where do i take the mug
faq.answer: Return the empty mug to Nori Pridedrift, who wanders Coldridge Valley in Dun Morogh selling his mornbrew.

faq.q: Is there a time limit to return the mug?
aliases: do i have to hurry back
faq.answer: There is no time limit. The first delivery of the Scalding Mornbrew had a strict timer to keep it piping hot, but you can return the empty mug at your own pace.

faq.q: Why does Nori care so much about an empty mug?
aliases: why does nori want the mug back
faq.answer: Quality mugs and steins are valuable barware in Dun Morogh. Nori points out that mugs do not grow on trees, and taverns cannot afford to lose drinkware to passing couriers.

faq.q: What quest leads directly into this one?
aliases: what comes before bring back the mug
faq.answer: This follows directly after Scalding Mornbrew Delivery, when Durnan drinks the beverage you brought him.

faq.q: Where can Durnan Furcutter be found?
faq.answer: Find Durnan Furcutter inside Anvilmar, the settlement dug into the mountain in Coldridge Valley. He sells cloth and leather armor.

angles.text: As a dwarf, you know that keeping a tavernkeeper's tankard can lead to a brawl. Returning Nori's mug is basic dwarven manners.
As a cook or brewer, you know good service ends only when the dishware is accounted for and returned to the kitchen.
